newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean opposition seeks labour reform bill delay.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean opposition seeks labour reform bill delay.

text.p: On the eve of a threatened general strike, South Korea's three main opposition parties on Thursday called for a delay in pushing through a controversial labour reform bill.
The ruling New Korea Party wants the bill passed during the current National Assembly session, which ends on December 18.

But a joint statement by the National Congress for New Politics, United Liberal Democrats and the Democratic Party said that timetable would not allow sufficient time to consider a bill that threatens industrial mayhem.
South Korea's two largest umbrella union groups have threatened walkouts, beginning with a four-hour stoppage on Friday, to protest the reforms.

"The government submitted the revised labour law on Tuesday, only seven days before the end of the session. It is impossible to seriously consider the law given the technical aspects of the revision and the shortage of time," the statement said.
It suggested an extraordinary parliamentary session be held in February to decide on the matter.
The first changes to South Korean labour legislation in 43 years would allow worker layoffs and flexible work hours, which organised labour sees as a threat to jobs.
Management objects to changes allowing multiple trade unions in each workplace, saying this will lead to increased militancy as unions compete for members.
